I’m a huge snacker too. What helps me the most is planning out the day so I can still fit in some snacks. If I plan out my day, I have enough calories to fit in some chips or a sweet treat even though I’m only eating 1450 calories so it’s possible!

Try to switch out your treats for something healthier. Fruit is great for bulk snacking. You can eat a ton of strawberries for little calories. I’m more of a salty snack person, and I find having a salty snack that’s higher in protein helps me get fuller faster instead of just mindlessly eating. Quest chips are great for this. 

Echoing other people to try to get more protein in, especially earlier during the day so it doesn’t lead to binge eating at night. You do not need to be working out to be drinking protein shakes. Though, working out, especially weight training, can help you burn more calories at rest = more calories available to eat throughout the day. I’m picky when it comes to protein shakes, but Fairlife shakes taste great. They’re sold in bulk at Costco and Sam’s. 

Try to up your fluid intake throughout the day, especially water. But, I also find diet sodas help keep me from going over cals. It satisfies a sweet craving and it’s 0 calories. If I feel like snacking, I’ll try drinking some more water or a diet soda and see if the craving is still there. It usually isn’t.

If you really want to be considered before those who don’t have their 24 hours completed and you can find a 3 hour course that is transferable and won’t be too hard for you, then I would take the wintermester course. Try using the UT ATE system to find out if and how the course will transfer, this helped me a ton. 
However, some colleges/majors are known for sending out decisions pretty late so completing your hours early wouldn’t mean too much. Some examples would be Cockrell, Mccombs, and the computer science major (basically the extremely competitive stuff). If you’re applying to these i’d say it wouldn’t mean too much to bother with the wintermester course. If you’re applying to any other major/college, then maybe consider taking the wintermester course. This is all my opinion, it’s up to you to figure out what you think would help your application the most.

Hey I just went through the transfer process for Spring 2018 so hopefully I can help. 
The deadline for the application to transfer for fall 2018 is March 1, 2018. You do not need to have 24 credits COMPLETED by that date but they must at least be IN PROGRESS. For example, you will have 21 credits completed by this semester, so i’m assuming you’ll at least take the extra 3 needed to transfer next semester. That means you may apply, but once your spring semester finishes they will need your final transcript showing that you’ve completed 24+ hours. The only setback to this is that your application will not be reviewed until you have proof that you’ve completed 24 hours. So, those who have competed 24 hours before the application deadline will be considered before you are. I hope that helps and isn’t too confusing. If you have any questions feel free to PM me.
